Worth a Revisit
Aug 2018 • Friends
Sixtysix is not far from our hotel of choice in Hanoi's Old Quarter, so invariably we head there for lunch at some time or another during our stay.

It is a smartly appointed restaurant, with an interesting collection of old black and white historical photographs of Hanoi framed on the walls.

We had Banana Flower Salad with Prawns and Pork, and Hanoi Spring Rolls with Noodles, with a small beer for me and a water for my friend.

At VND 265650 Sixtysix is mid-range pricing for this area.

Appealing from afar, but far from appealing
Mar 2018 • Couples
Decided to treat ourselves after an evening of hotel snafus and disappointment. Little did we know that the biggest disappointment was yet to come.

From outside it looks stylish, polished, and the lure of clay pots and wine was too much for my girlfriend to pass up. We came in, saw the reasonable mains and decided to eat. We ordered the crab spring rolls, which were, in fairness, quite good. 

Our food came to us in a state of temperature confusion. Our main dishes - for me a pork belly and prawn curry and for my girlfriend a seafood clay pot - were both fine. However, the vegetables were cold and the rice barely tepid. In addition, the restaurant added a 15% service charge, perhaps to offset the cost of keeping rice at just below room temperature. Disappointing. The most expensive meal we’ve had in Vietnam and yet the worst. I’d rather have eaten at the pho joint across the road.

Overpriced and average
Aug 2017 • Couples
From the outside this looks like a really nice restaurant, and the decor is very stylish inside. However our experience didn't reflect this.

A table had just freed up when we arrived so they sat us down, cleared away half of the dirty plates and left the other half on the side of the table for the next 20 minutes before they took our order, not replacing the cutlery until AFTER our food arrived, when I explicitly asked.

I ordered a la carte, a crab soup, duck with orange and a Campari and orange cocktail.

However, the menu is misleading, as when you order one of the more expensive dishes (as I did) expecting a full meal, you're served a very small amount of meat/fish with absolutely no rice or vegetables on the side. A small pot of additional rice (which is basically free in Vietnam) costs 25K more, which they did not tell us when we requested a small amount of rice to go with the dish. 

The soup was gloopy and there were about 5 spoonfuls in total, and the Campari and Orange came in a tumbler glass less than a third full with no ice or garnish or anything.

The menu items are vastly overpriced for Vietnam, even for a capital city, and this all comes as well as the 15% involuntary service charge they throw on when you get the bill- which in some countries I would expect but has never happened in our month travelling Vietnam.

Food was average at best and I would definitely NOT recommend this restaurant, there are much better value and quality Vietnamese meals available in Hanoi.
